doc: Detection duties of the observation-driven runtime. Each is a producer (the only polling), a signal with max_age, and a resolver role. `replaces` names the retired detector units. Exit codes: 0 GREEN, 2 RED, anything else a failed observation that ages to UNKNOWN.

duties.name: ci
duties.covers: GitHub Actions result for the remote commit

duties.name: dispatch
duties.covers: a wake left open (started/unknown) longer than 30 minutes

duties.name: egress-mesh-home
duties.covers: tailscale exit-node egress for mesh-home (one client; split from the aggregate egress duty so one unreachable client does not hide the others)

duties.name: egress-note3
duties.covers: tailscale exit-node egress for note3 (adb path)

duties.name: egress-imac-rozalia
duties.covers: egress for imac-rozalia; UNKNOWN while the imac is off the LAN (resolver network)

duties.name: guard-bytes
duties.covers: installed host guard bytes equal the reviewed target

duties.name: boot-admission
duties.covers: Boot admission failure, containment latch and producer startup

duties.name: restore-readiness
duties.covers: the host can restore the plant

duties.name: observer-checks
duties.covers: the observer check inventory

duties.name: omp-db
duties.covers: omp agent database integrity

duties.name: devto
duties.covers: DEV.to threads observed and delivered

duties.name: pub-devto-watch-delivery
duties.covers: the installed devto watcher returns its delivery failure as RED (2) and its unreadable scan as UNKNOWN (3), the two codes the devto duty routes

duties.name: devto-article-duplication
duties.covers: no published DEV.to article repeats a paragraph verbatim

duties.name: pub-index-self-claims
duties.covers: the DEV.to index page's published counts match the account

duties.name: pub-account-count-claims
duties.covers: every count a published page states about the DEV account matches the account

duties.name: pub-privacy-scan
duties.covers: no live or draft DEV.to body, title, tag, card description, reply or the account's own published profile breaks the private/public rule list

duties.name: pub-publish-privacy-gate
duties.covers: the DEV write path refuses a draft that breaks the private/public rule before the write

duties.name: pub-plant-state-claims
duties.covers: every figure a published post states about the plant's own running state matches the plant

duties.name: budget
duties.covers: token and quota windows; RED or UNKNOWN holds spontaneous wakes

duties.name: budget-consistency
duties.covers: budget account consistency, freshness, and pinned routing under RED budget and weekly quota pacing

duties.name: budget-opencode-go
duties.covers: the opencode-go weekly allowance window (go-a): remaining, burn per hour, projected end and ledger selections; UNKNOWN when unmeasured

duties.name: budget-codex
duties.covers: the codex-a 5h and 7d windows (openai-codex): spent-window LOW and UNKNOWN when a window is not FRESH; burn is not judged

duties.name: stats-refresh
duties.covers: omp stats.db freshness for mishe stats: runs omp stats --json every 15 min under MemoryMax=2G and goes RED when stats.db is still older than 30 min after a successful refresh; UNKNOWN when the refresh fails or times out

duties.name: signal-coverage
duties.covers: the signal of signals (Ilya DM #303234): every registered signal has a live producer, a subscriber and a response — unmeasured (never observed past the store's grace), stale freshness stamp, RED or UNKNOWN reading unchanged past 2*max_age, unheard orphan files, failed mishe-producer units and budget accounts with no measuring duty; unattended-red (Ilya DM #303254): a RED older than 15 min with no owner-role wake active since it turned, named with its owner, so a RED standing in a window with no mind awake reaches health and the resolver within one producer cadence instead of the hour reoffer; names itself RED when its own producer missed cadence, UNKNOWN when the registry is unreadable; wake_on state so only a RED/UNKNOWN verdict wakes a subscriber (steward resolves; health also subscribes so an unattended RED wakes the standing caretaker through the ordinary path trigger)

duties.name: budget-view-mapping
duties.covers: the budget window shows the engine each mind runs on: the file's own routing selection and the live ledger

duties.name: root-fs-stall
duties.covers: root-drive fsync stalls of 5 s or more in the last 900 s, from the dual-probe mirror; the signal was registered with no producer and went UNKNOWN on 2026-11-14 11:01Z

duties.name: root-fs-band
duties.covers: root-drive sub-threshold band: probes >= 1 s in the last 30 min at least twice the 6 h median and at least 5, the lead the 5 s root-fs-stall RED cannot give

duties.name: inotify-headroom
duties.covers: this uid's inotify instances against fs.inotify.max_user_instances; RED at 85%. Added 2026-11-24 after the user manager exhausted 512 and the revive service failed with EMFILE

duties.name: root-migration-bulk
duties.covers: the root-drive migration bulk copy (step 6 first pass, docs/root-fs-migration-plan.md): GREEN when bulk.log records 'all done rc=0', RED when a tree failed or the log stopped advancing mid-pass, UNKNOWN while a tree is still copying, so completion is event-observable instead of polled

duties.name: host-capacity
duties.covers: memory/CPU/IO pressure and anon split, admission for optional work

duties.name: ilya-telegram-bot
duties.covers: the fine-tuned Telegram bot service is alive and its long-poll loop is advancing: RED when the unit is not active or its heartbeat is stale, UNKNOWN when systemd or the heartbeat cannot be read

duties.name: lzhezalia-bot
duties.covers: the Rosalia imitation bot service is alive and its long-poll loop is advancing: RED when the unit is not active or its heartbeat is stale, UNKNOWN when systemd or the heartbeat cannot be read

duties.name: darinci-bot
duties.covers: the Daria imitation bot service is alive and its long-poll loop is advancing: RED when the unit is not active or its heartbeat is stale, UNKNOWN when systemd or the heartbeat cannot be read

duties.name: delivery-requests
duties.covers: a delivery admission held by a dead owner, or a delivery request left UNKNOWN; observed between wakes, not only at consume

duties.name: tape-lock
duties.covers: the plant-wide tape/task lock can be taken; a stuck holder blocks every wall, task and tape write

duties.name: readings
duties.covers: bounded acquisition of the retained Senses inventory; source-specific unknowns stay visible, failed/missing/stale scans remain UNKNOWN

duties.name: view-readability
duties.covers: every role's top and bottom pane renders as human-readable text: no JSON, dict reprs, escaped newlines, raw epoch numbers or private paths; unrenderable or missing views stay UNKNOWN

duties.name: build-cache-stubs
duties.covers: the shared cargo build cache holds only ELF installed binaries: RED names any text stub a delivery check would test against (2026-11-16, 08547645); UNKNOWN when the cache cannot be read

duties.name: components
duties.covers: every promoted component still matches its ledger and the live $SITE/bin install: components.verify is GREEN and, where consumers still read $SITE/bin/NAME before component-deploy step 3, its sha256 equals the promoted bytes, so a promotion and a later hand install cannot drift apart silently; RED names the component and the differing digests, UNKNOWN when no component is promoted or the detector cannot be imported

duties.name: bound-evidence
duties.covers: a bound evidence file is still the bytes its outcome recorded, and the bytes it bound are recoverable: the check reports the rows writable now (no clause applied), read-only now but changed after binding, and the bound paths missing, then asks of each lost row whether SITE/bound-bytes/<digest> still holds bytes hashing to the recorded digest. RED when a publishing root keeps no copy of the bytes it binds (a pin advance that contains d5e9730f starts the store), when a root naming the store keeps none, or when a row published after the store was live has no held copy; the mode not surviving a path replace is reported as a design fact, not the verdict, because the copy makes drift over held bytes recoverable and provable. UNKNOWN when no root carrying the clause could be probed. The answer comes from SITE/records directly, not from the published coverage report the three retired checks read (2026-11-17)

duties.name: push-lag
duties.covers: local main reaches GitHub within a quarter hour (checks/push-lag.py --repo: a normal push finishes in under a minute, and two commits made with a hooks-disabled commit command sat unpublished 16 min under the old two-hour bound on 2026-11-17): RED when the oldest unpushed commit is older, or main has diverged; UNKNOWN when the remote cannot be read

duties.name: main-publication
duties.covers: local main reaches origin/main without depending on the post-commit hook (checks/main-publication.py --repo: a commit made with a hooks-disabled command was never pushed, so 4290a757 sat unpublished 14 min until a mind read, 2026-11-17): the duty fast-forwards origin/main itself when it is a strict ancestor of local main and names how many commits it published; RED when the push fails, main has diverged, or local main is behind; UNKNOWN when the remote or local HEAD cannot be read and when the run's own budget runs out mid-step (the check enforces a 240 s budget itself: local git calls 15 s, fetch and push 60 s, each call clamped to the remaining budget and a past deadline exits 3 naming the step; the push path makes 12 calls, so the old 240 s duty timeout killed it silently while the check still had work to report; timeout 270 s now exceeds the check's own bound)

duties.name: next-due-armed
duties.covers: due-time wakes are armed for this site: RED when there is a recorded due time and no timer in this site's next-due namespace, or the units-installed marker is missing; UNKNOWN when next-due.json or systemd cannot be read

duties.name: signal-expiry
duties.covers: stored OK readings are retired after their freshness deadlines even when a next-due timer exists: RED when a stored OK is over five minutes past its deadline; UNKNOWN when registry, reading or freshness stamp evidence is missing or unreadable

duties.name: next-due-churn
duties.covers: the scheduler keeps the pending next-due timer instead of restarting it on every arm (commit 606330ad): pairs each of THIS plant's mishe-next-due timer starts in the last five minutes with a due handler run and is RED when more than 10 starts had none (156 starts against 1 run measured at release 4f0962ae, 2026-11-18 09:47Z); a neighbour plant sharing the user systemd manager is excluded by --home, and arm.py tags timer names with the site home so neither plant stops the other's timer; UNKNOWN when the journal is unreadable or no timer was started in the window, since next-due-armed owns whether a timer exists

duties.name: overdue-intention
duties.covers: due intentions are served:RED when an intention is more than 15 minutes past due with no wake of its role since then and no GREEN budget hold explaining it; UNKNOWN when intentions, the wake ledger or a budget signal cannot be read or is stale; HELD (not a fault) when a spontaneous intention is held by a RED budget signal

duties.name: units-after-trip
duties.covers: enabled mishe-* units left dead after a containment trip: RED with the names and minutes dead while the tripped latch is absent (the drop-in's ConditionPathExists skips a restart that would otherwise succeed once the latch clears); with --act each dead unit is started once per dead episode after a 120 s grace; GREEN while the latch is present or no enabled unit is dead; UNKNOWN when systemctl or journalctl cannot be read

duties.name: unit-restart-churn
duties.covers: a watched user unit (light-cycle-monitor.service) restarting in a loop before systemd's start limit trips: RED when it restarted at least 3 times within 15 min (Restart=always, a SIGKILL never enters failed so OnFailure does not fire); GREEN otherwise; UNKNOWN when systemctl cannot be read or the state cannot be saved

duties.name: inkling-upstream-timeout
duties.covers: the Inkling proxy (inkling-proxy.service) reporting upstream TimeoutError to its callers in the last 15 min: RED on any such line (2026-11-27 18:24 timeouts had no detector; the pub wake was lost at 18:54); GREEN otherwise; UNKNOWN when journalctl cannot be read

duties.name: inkling-inference-probe
duties.covers: the local Inkling route (proxy on 127.0.0.1:8081) answering a 4-token completion within 20 s: RED on a silent route (no answer in 20 s, which the 180 s wake watchdog would only report after the 1800 s cap), a refused connection or a non-200 reply; GREEN otherwise; UNKNOWN when the body is not a chat completion. Exists because the 2026-11-27 18:51 to 18:54 pub hang passed /v1/models and /health and logged no proxy TimeoutError

duties.name: work-trial
duties.covers: Bounded useful-work 6h/24h reports and retained final checkpoint validity; corrupt or interrupted evidence stays UNKNOWN.

duties.name: work-watch
duties.covers: Deterministic evidence/deadline sweep independent of next-due rearming; failure or missing sweep output remains UNKNOWN within five minutes.

duties.name: audio-hint-livingroom
duties.covers: living-room microphone hint window: one row per cadence; UNKNOWN when the mic or transcriber fails

duties.name: audio-listener-coverage
duties.covers: resident living-room listener heartbeat: GREEN when its status is fresh and at least half of wall time is observed, RED under 50 %, UNKNOWN when the status is stale, missing, stopped, restarting, suspended or warming up. max_age sits above every + the timer's per-period jitter + clock accuracy (105 + 26 + 5) so a healthy run never reads expired between samples

duties.name: voice-clone-ready
duties.covers: voice.clone.ready: clone model file, mesh-voice-clone.socket (the daemon is on demand), the daemon socket and a no-sound synthesis probe while warm or every 6 h when cold, with bounded self-healing

duties.name: household-camera-livingroom
duties.covers: living-room webcam brightness grid, one row every 150 s (kept under the unit start budget); a blind lens (covered, dark or flat) is status blind, recorded and exits 2 (RED, observed); the V4L2 input held by another process on every bounded attempt exits 4 (UNKNOWN, input missing, unit succeeds); any other failed capture exits 1 (crash)

duties.name: household-camera-bedroom
duties.covers: bedroom Mac camera brightness grid every four minutes; a blind lens is status blind, recorded and exits 2 (RED, observed); an unreachable Mac exits 4 (UNKNOWN, input missing, unit succeeds); a local crash or config error exits 1 (crash)

duties.name: frame-label-tick
duties.covers: calibration photos to Ilya's own chat: sweeps frames older than 24 h, applies his reply-to labels, and on a noticeable camera change sends at most 3 photos per 8 h (cap persisted before send); sends nothing otherwise

duties.name: map-render
duties.covers: re-renders the apartment map (svg, text, map-state.json) from the latest evidence, hypothesis priors and corrections so sprites move without a senses wake; RED/UNKNOWN only when the renderer itself fails

duties.name: rssi-motion
duties.covers: study (experiment rssi-motion): does the Redmi10 RSSI jitter over 15-minute buckets track camera-seen activity better than the RSSI level, against a whole-day-shift null; writes senses/map/rssi-motion.json (phone vantage) and senses/map/rssi-motion-router-station.json (router-station vantage, read from the senses archive senses/map/router-station-redmi10.jsonl that each run refreshes); GREEN means a fresh SIGNAL or NO_SIGNAL verdict was computed for the phone vantage, UNKNOWN when the camera table, the phone log or its newest RSSI row is missing or stale; router-station is UNKNOWN until its joined count reaches the minimum

duties.name: rssi-history
duties.covers: one age-stamped Redmi10 Wi-Fi RSSI and BLE-count row appended to senses/map/rssi-history.jsonl every two minutes (120 s keeps the timer under the host start limit of 3 per 5 min); GREEN while the newest row is under three minutes old, UNKNOWN when the writer stops or fails

duties.name: household-phones
duties.covers: Note3 sensor sample and Redmi10 stream freshness with raw light and accelerometer; a stale or missing phone exits UNKNOWN

duties.name: household-daylight
duties.covers: per-room daylight curve (UTC hour median luma, lamp steps removed) rebuilt from signatures.jsonl every ten minutes; no usable signature rows or a crash exits UNKNOWN (never an empty GREEN curve), an hour without ok samples stays null

duties.name: household-features
duties.covers: hourly house-level feature store (features/house-hourly.jsonl) built from the household samplers: one row per complete UTC hour, derived numbers per room and device, absent source = no key (UNKNOWN), never zero; no readable source file exits UNKNOWN. The long-lived record for prediction nets; never trimmed by retention

duties.name: house-predictions
duties.covers: house prediction log: each run writes forecasts for the next hour and the same hour tomorrow (baselines last-value and same-hour) BEFORE the hour, scores earlier ones when their hour reaches the feature store, and refreshes the scoreboard the house window prints; no feature store or a store newer than 4 h old absent exits UNKNOWN and makes no forecast, an unmeasured hour is unobserved, never zero

duties.name: household-activity
duties.covers: household activity.json every ten minutes: 15-min per-room change buckets, lights events, the quiet block and the rhythm line (provisional, not validated), plus hourly audio level; no ok signature rows exits UNKNOWN

duties.name: rust-plan-progress
duties.covers: the rust-plan investigation is making progress: its canonical wall exists and is inside its bound, and the plan document is present and non-empty; a missing or stale wall is RED, an unreadable observation is UNKNOWN, and a producer that stops running ages the signal to UNKNOWN

duties.name: network-probe
duties.covers: home connectivity: gateway and public-resolver latency and loss, DNS and HTTPS timing (rows in network/probe.jsonl); RED when the internet is unreachable, UNKNOWN when the probe cannot run

duties.name: network-probe-shape
duties.covers: the newest network-probe row (network/probe.jsonl) is at most 15 min old and carries the 0.2.0 host block (cpu_some10, io_some10); RED when a fresh row lacks it (the 0.2.0 probe is not what writes the reading) or when every reachable internet site lacks the lookup_ms name-lookup timing, UNKNOWN when the log has no readable newest row, the row is stale, or lookup_ms is not numeric

duties.name: network-speed
duties.covers: the bounded speed readings (network/speed.jsonl for the 5 MB download, network/speed-up.jsonl for the 2 MB upload): one of each, only 02-05 local and at most every 12 h; the download is UNKNOWN when the last attempt failed or the last good reading is older than 36 h; the upload is UNKNOWN when its last attempt failed, its last good reading is older than 36 h, or no attempt was recorded during the off-peak window while the producer ran; RED when the duty itself cannot run

duties.name: network-router
duties.covers: the router's read-only Wi-Fi and uplink reading (rows in network/router.jsonl): per-device signal and rate (hashed id, household device name), WAN state, router uptime; UNKNOWN when ssh to the router fails or its output is unreadable, RED only when the duty itself cannot run

duties.name: network-singbox-stream
duties.covers: the router's sing-box log lines collected read-only every 2 min into analysis/router-singbox-stream.log (deduped, UTC-stamped) so probe timing can be joined over hours; its status file records the last attempt and last success; UNKNOWN when the router read fails or the collector has not run within 10 min

duties.name: network-router-load
duties.covers: the router's own load/free-RAM self-limit (the 5-minute average above 1.0 or free RAM below 120 MB the producer backs off on and the window prints, from router_load in network/router.jsonl): RED when an unbroken run of over-limit readings spans at least 30 minutes with no gap over 20 minutes, UNKNOWN when no reading carries load in the last six hours or the newest is older than 15 minutes, GREEN otherwise with a short breach named in the message

duties.name: network-uplink
duties.covers: the WAN receive-drop rate (eth0 rx_dropped per hour, from the router readings in network/router.jsonl), rx_errors above zero, and the physical WAN link (negotiated speed/duplex and carrier drops from the same read); RED above 400 drops/h over a full 1.8 h span, on any rx_errors, or on three carrier drops inside the two-hour window, UNKNOWN when the newest router reading is missing or older than 15 min, the rx_dropped counter reset, or the read carries no physical link state or no negotiated speed

duties.name: network-vpn
duties.covers: the router's VPN tunnel (sing-box process and tun0 link, from the router readings in network/router.jsonl): RED when a fresh reading shows sing-box NOT running or tun0 down or absent, UNKNOWN when there is no fresh reading, the router process list was unreadable or the link state is unknown

duties.name: network-devices
duties.covers: the per-device ping reading (rows in network/devices.jsonl, five pings each to the named household devices, currently iMac-Rozalia): a row per run, a failed ping recorded as failed; RED only when the producer itself cannot run, UNKNOWN otherwise (the detector judges the rows)

duties.name: network-device-reach
duties.covers: the newest per-device ping row in network/devices.jsonl: GREEN when every named device answered within 15 min; UNKNOWN when no row is fresh, a device's ping failed or could not run (named), or the row is from the future; slowness is printed, not judged; never RED from this detector

duties.name: network-wifi
duties.covers: the Wi-Fi channel, noise-floor and transmit-counter sub-reading from the router's read-only iwinfo and iwpriv passes in network/router.jsonl: RED when a fresh reading carries impossible channel or noise values, UNKNOWN when no fresh reading carries the sub-reading, a field is missing, or any radio's transmit counters are missing (one dead iwpriv must not look like a quiet band), GREEN when both bands report plausible numbers and counters

duties.name: network-window
duties.covers: the outer tmux window plants:network exists and runs tools/network_view.py; RED when missing or dead, RED when the running copy of the view differs from the view's files on disk (or it never reported its copy) with the exact respawn command and the copy's own load time, RED when the visible pane says WINDOW ERROR (a live process drawing no readings), GREEN for a difference within 30 s of the newest file write because the view reloads on its next 10 s redraw, UNKNOWN when tmux or git cannot be read or the pane text cannot be captured

duties.name: network-progress
duties.covers: the network mind keeps improving network visibility: its wall is under six hours old and network files were committed within 48 hours; RED when it has gone quiet, UNKNOWN when git cannot be read

duties.name: wake-waste
duties.covers: wakes that did real work and were thrown away: a wake in the last two hours ended by timeout, or without a yield after a stream of a megabyte or more; RED rolls the losses up per candidate (engine/model/account) with cause class, count, roles, minutes and size so the resolver fixes timeout policy, wake scope or engine use; UNKNOWN when the routing ledger cannot be read

duties.name: wake-wait-stall
duties.covers: a hard-cap wake in the last two hours whose last wait still held a running subagent job: RED names the wake, role, job id, type, model and duration from a bounded 4 MB tail of the retained stream; UNKNOWN when the routing ledger or a required wake stream cannot be read and no running wait is confirmed

duties.name: wake-compaction-loop
duties.covers: an active wake (stream written in the last 15 min) that has overflowed its context at least twice (length-stopped turns plus context-full compactions) without issuing mishe yield: RED names the wake, role and counts from a bounded 4 MB tail; UNKNOWN when the wake directory is missing; failed-mishe-wake-* only fires at process exit, so this is the earlier signal

duties.name: wake-memory-floor
duties.covers: the declared memory floor of every running wake and producer: a daemon-reload re-writes the protected drop-in's 1G onto running units, throttling the engine at the mark until its timeout throws the work away; RED names the unit still below the floor after a persistence window, so recurrence is visible within two minutes instead of waiting for host memory PSI to move

duties.name: human-inbound-relayed
duties.covers: the human's own inbound lines reach the operator chat: the mishe-human-inbound-relay timer relays each new line of voice-in.log from a byte cursor; RED when an unrelayed human line is older than the limit (relay stopped), UNKNOWN when the log, cursor or voice receiver cannot be read; this duty only observes, the timer does the relay

duties.name: human-typed-relayed
duties.covers: the human's typed lines in his interactive session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/<repo-slug>/*.jsonl) reach the operator chat: the relay timer advances per-file byte cursors and DMs each new human-typed line to operator; RED when an unrelayed human line is older than the limit, immediately when the relay timer itself is inactive, or when the relay service's last one-shot run failed (both missing/stopped relay forms are visible before a line goes stale), UNKNOWN when the transcripts, cursor, timer or service state cannot be read. The 2026-11-19 Sonnet-ban lift arrived only in this channel, invisible to every mind until traced by hand

duties.name: rust-measurement
duties.covers: the cache-miss full fold of the senses and genome tapes, measured in fresh processes, plus the installed Rust binaries checked against their install records and this release's crate source: GREEN only when both roles' Python reader stays under 5 CPU-s and peak RSS under 200 MB (the Rust slice stays closed) and every installed binary matches, with each fold's Rust-children CPU and total CPU recorded beside the reader reading (plan 10.55); RED when the reader CPU or RSS trigger is hit (the slice may reopen), or when installed bytes no longer match their record or a crate's source drifted past the installed commit; UNKNOWN when the host guard, the fold or the installed-byte provenance cannot give a reading

duties.name: initiatives-health
duties.covers: an initiative owned by health in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-senses
duties.covers: an initiative owned by senses in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-steward
duties.covers: an initiative owned by steward in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: experiments-lifecycle
duties.covers: experiments.json lists each experiment with a status and decision date: a running experiment past its decision date is AMBER, a week past is RED; a tracked file named experiment, exploratory or pilot that no registry entry owns is AMBER; UNKNOWN when the registry is missing or invalid or git cannot list the tracked files

duties.name: code-health-lint
duties.covers: ruff (pyflakes and syntax rules) findings per rule against code-health-baseline.json: any rule above its baseline is RED, below it AMBER until the baseline is lowered; UNKNOWN when ruff is not installed in SITE/code-health-venv, times out or prints undecodable output

duties.name: code-health-types
duties.covers: mypy error count over src/ against code-health-baseline.json: above baseline is RED, below it AMBER until the baseline is lowered; UNKNOWN when mypy is not installed, times out or the baseline is missing

duties.name: code-health-coverage
duties.covers: line coverage of src/ measured weekly by running the suite under coverage.py: more than half a point below the baseline is RED, above it AMBER until the baseline is raised; UNKNOWN when coverage is not installed, the suite fails under coverage or the report is older than nine days

duties.name: initiatives-system1
duties.covers: an initiative owned by system1 in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-genome
duties.covers: an initiative owned by genome in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-field-review
duties.covers: an initiative owned by field-review in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-pub
duties.covers: an initiative owned by pub in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: initiatives-rust-plan
duties.covers: an initiative owned by rust-plan in SITE/initiatives.json is past its due time and its acceptance check says not done; UNKNOWN when the register is missing or a check cannot be evaluated (a charter-less owner's item is reported UNKNOWN by the steward duty, not here)

duties.name: pin-lag
duties.covers: the running pin trails committed main: GREEN under 60 minutes, or while a live promotion record (a non-terminal phase no older than red_age) is moving this HEAD; AMBER (exit 1, 60 min to 3 h) and RED (exit 2, beyond) both read RED so a lagging pin wakes its resolver early, with the stage and reason of the newest delivery run; UNKNOWN when the pin is missing or not a commit of this clone

duties.name: review-backlog
duties.covers: delivered releases whose asynchronous review has not merged are visible: GREEN when every delivered record's review merged, RED (exit 2) once any delivered release owes a review — the detail carries the count, the next retry rung and the newest reviewer failure reason, so a spent reviewer quota is seen instead of hidden behind the ladder, and it names the records that cannot recover on their own (ladder exhausted, no rung past the grace, or a rung that never fired) — UNKNOWN when no release record can be read. There is no intermediate code: an undeclared non-zero exit would publish UNKNOWN with the reason 'check exit N' and fail the producer unit (measured 2026-11-17 22:29Z)

duties.name: pin-delivery
duties.covers: the outcome of the newest pin promotion: GREEN delivered and the pointer names it, or still running; RED check-failed, check-mutated, rolled-back or UNKNOWN naming the sha, phase, failure and the last failing test line; UNKNOWN with no record, an unreadable record, a pointer that disagrees or a promotion stuck over an hour

duties.name: delivery-cadence
duties.covers: the automatic moving-pin cadence runs: it starts one promotion when the pin trails a settled HEAD, skips while a delivery, heal or patch gate is running, and honours the settle and retry bounds; the signal is GREEN while the cadence keeps running and ages to UNKNOWN if it stops, so a stalled cadence is observed rather than silent

duties.name: commit-risk
duties.covers: advisory commit-risk class for recent commits (path rules first, the decision model only for the mixed residual): UNKNOWN when the decision provider is not configured or residual commits stay unanswered while the daily cap has room; never gates delivery

duties.name: repo-change
duties.covers: System 0 repo-change signal (initiative repo-change-signal): on each run it reads the commits on the checkout since the oldest subscriber cursor, drops internal-only noise, names the reader docs that mention each changed source path, and publishes value = newest commit with per-subscriber deltas (pub, docs) in its detail; it also publishes repo-change-pub (value = newest reader-meaningful commit, not docs-only, the only signal pub wakes on) and repo-change-system1 (value = newest commit touching src, tools or duties, the only signal system1 wakes on). The resolver is docs, the one reader of the raw signal: system1 is no longer subscribed to it (2026-11-21: 24 raw wakes in 4 h, all docs-only, all verified). UNKNOWN when git or the reader corpus cannot be read; never GREEN on missing evidence; it calls no model and wakes no one itself

duties.name: system1-savings
duties.covers: P4 measured System One savings over the trailing 24 h, System 0 only (no provider call): wake starts per day by trigger class, wakes avoided by a live gate, projected skip and changed-rate of same-dossier wakes against all wakes, decision calls and spend. UNKNOWN when the wake-gate ledger is missing or corrupt or the decision budget is stale; never RED, since savings are not a failure

duties.name: memory-samples
duties.covers: memory PSI avg10, anon memory and charged memory (Cached + Slab), one row every three minutes in the signal sample store (a 60 s timer hit the host StartLimitBurst=3 per 5 min and failed on the fourth start); a gap is a gap, UNKNOWN when the store or the reading fails

duties.name: hold-state
duties.covers: the site's hold file: no hold, a hold whose named writer (a promotion pid, a flip pid) is alive, RED when that writer is gone, RED when an anonymous manual or boot hold stands longer than its --max-age (3600 s, refreshed by re-running `mishe hold on`), and one RED after such a hold ends with no recorded disposition. With --release this producer also removes a stale hold (dead writer, or anonymous past --max-age) when the dispatch lock is free and the host guard is not tripped, then reports one RED with the disposition to the operator (operator decision 2026-11-19: nobody else can, a hold suppresses wake starts). A hold suppresses wake starts, so its own fault cannot wake anyone while it stands: this producer runs on a timer and its verdict is visible in the signals and after the wake resumes

duties.name: disk-budget
duties.covers: the disks Mishe needs and the bytes it owns: RED when root free space is under 30 GiB (the host guard trips at 10 GiB and re-arms at 12), /var/tmp free under 10 GiB, the checkout plus site home over 64 GiB, or the releases tree over 2 GiB; UNKNOWN when a reading cannot be taken. Over its ceiling, the releases tree is pruned to the live set plus the newest 8 (runtime/current is protected by name; 40 removals per run, reversible with git worktree add). Sizes are scanned at idle IO priority and cached 30 minutes. wake_on=state wakes health only on RED or UNKNOWN

duties.name: footprint
duties.covers: honest footprint: latest anon and charged memory and PSI avg10 read from the sample store beside each other, with the newest sample's age; UNKNOWN when any of the three has no sample in the last 15 minutes. wake_on=state: the reading drifts every sample, so it wakes health only when the reading is not OK (silence, expiry or a failed read), never on the drift itself

duties.name: view-window-coverage
duties.covers: every tools/*_view.py has an entry in operator/window-registry.json and a live (not dead) outer plants window running it (docs/outer-windows.md rule: a view has a window); RED names each view without a registry entry or without a live window and the command that closes it; UNKNOWN when tmux is unreachable, its rows are malformed, the registry is missing or no view file is found

duties.name: outer-pane-code
duties.covers: every release-pinned outer view pane runs the script bytes at the current pin: the live pane's cwd names its release, the registry names its view, and the check compares content so an unchanged promotion is not a false RED; RED names the window, its release, the pin and the respawn command when a long-lived pane keeps superseded code (senses found plants:senses-map stale for days through several promotions on 2026-11-20); panes restored from the working tree are not release-pinned and are not judged here; a missing window belongs to view-window-coverage; UNKNOWN when tmux, the registry, the pin, a pane cwd or a script cannot be read

duties.name: tmux-restorer
duties.covers: runs tools/tmux_restore.py --apply so a missing or dead registered window (restore: true in operator/window-registry.json) comes back without a hand; it never types into a pane; RED when a restore command failed, UNKNOWN when the registry or its sessions cannot be read

This duty's own covers said retire it when Ilya lifts the ban; kept around it would RED the moment steward routes a Sonnet model, which the human just allowed. Routing and spend stay covered by the budget duties and the routing ledger (the 11-11 retirement debc8d3d set the same precedent)
pane/tmux liveness and the core supervisor's own observer; there are no panes and no resident supervisor
replaced by the owed check, due intentions and the next-due timer; a role that stops being woken shows as an open or aged dispatch

no resident runtime can lag the checkout; a wake pins its release at start and doctor compares installed units with the pin. The producer's age detector was removed with it (2026-11-17): it aged checks/substrate-watch.json, which froze UNKNOWN at 2026-11-04 when the module went, so it could only ever report a stale snapshot nobody writes. A producer that stops is now visible through its duty signal's max_age (arm expires it and wakes the resolver; tests/test_signal_store_freshness.py), a dead unit through units-after-trip.py, and the pin and host guard bytes through pin-integrity.py and guard-bytes-drift.py
role residents; roles remain as registry data and are woken by trigger

the recovery runtime's incident outbox and evaluation reported to resident minds; pressure is now the host-capacity signal and failures route through mishe-failed. recovery_io remains as manual tooling (accept/evaluate), not as units

the duty was dropped on 2026-11-15 (f1341a56) because pin-lag reads the same lag with one threshold, but the check file outlived it unscheduled: no timer ran it, and its 30-minute limit sits below the measured promotion duration (20.9, 28.4, 35.8, 47.9, 58.9 min in the records under SITE/work/releases), so it could only fire while a promotion was legitimately in flight, and it made check-scheduler-coverage FAILING-UNOBSERVED on every run. The check and its test were removed (2026-11-17). The scheduled pin-lag duty replaces it: same comparison, GREEN under 60 minutes, AMBER to 3 h, RED beyond, and it prints the newest delivery stage and failure. It also reads a promotion of HEAD that is still running (a live work/releases record in a non-terminal phase) as progress: GREEN with the run's stage while the lag is under --red-age, RED past it

all three read the plant's published coverage report SITE/checks/initiative.json, whose only producer was deleted with the pane runtime (943276d9, 2026-11-04). The report's last publication is 2026-11-03T21:37Z, so writable-bound-evidence and coverage-gap-remedy returned UNKNOWN (exit 3, report 1152917 s stale on 2026-11-17) and ledger-band-second-reader's premise, the coverage reader initiative.collect publishing a band per row, was deleted with the same commit. None was ever registered in this repository's duties.json, so no verdict they produced was read. Retired with their tests on 2026-11-17. The writable population stays reported by checks/bound-evidence-clause-enforcement.py, which reads SITE/records directly and measured 176 writable and 31 defeated rows that day. The remedy question (does a lost row carry a published remedy) now has no detector; it is named here rather than dropped, and would need a reader of the record store, not of the deleted report
